output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by the vendor's edge rule pack update on 3 March, not by release 6.14. A new rule, AUTO-LIB-17, blocks any password-login request from the app's networking library when it has no edge session cookie. It started blocking at 10:41 UTC and now blocks about 9,600 requests a day. The blocked requests come from real Android installs: 92% of them had logged in successfully before. The added failures are all 403 rejections on password logins, and they appear at the same minute on every app version, including old ones. They show no link to OS version or the March security patch. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. The same edge change explains why a 6.14 rollback would not help. Credential stuffing, as measured, is not the cause either, because bot traffic doesn't emit app telemetry. Next steps: ask Corvane to set the new rules to log-only on the mobile password-login path, keeping the other protections on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Don't roll back 6.14, don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't change the KPI definition. The call-volume link is plausible but unproven because the reason codes are unreliable.
